project.name: HDF5
project.commit_note: Stage 02 inspected the staged ARVO workspace checkout at `966454aac1231da7209ef81c11055d3312181f99`, whose line map matches the cited vulnerable source and the crashing hunk in `patch.diff`. Sample metadata separately records `875fb3e70a0d9b4e71b4fac5c31badc012359618` / `ce53bc020d37e10a06a59501c45f1ab82539f0c5` as the vulnerable and fixed commits.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42522531 (hdf5): Heap-buffer-overflow READ 5 found by fuzz target h5_extended_fuzzer [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42522531
bug_description.normalized: The staged `poc` is an HDF5 file that `H5Fopen` accepts far enough to verify the root group and later call `H5Dopen2(..., "dsetname")`. During root-group symbol-table heap loading, `H5HL__hdr_deserialize` decodes the local-heap data-block size from the file header and `H5HL__cache_datablock_deserialize` allocates an 88-byte `heap->dblk_image` and copies the attacker-controlled heap bytes into it. Later, root-group lookup for the fixed dataset name `dsetname` enters `H5G__stab_lookup` and `H5B_find`, which passes a symbol-table key offset into `H5G__node_cmp3`. `H5HL_offset_into` verifies only that the selected offset is inside the heap buffer and returns a pointer into the copied heap bytes; it does not ensure the remaining heap suffix is NUL-terminated. `H5G__node_cmp3` then calls `HDstrcmp(udata->name, s)` on that interior pointer as though it were an unbounded C string. On the saved Stage 01 run, the left-side heap suffix used by the compare is not terminated before the end of the 88-byte buffer, so the intercepted `strcmp` reads 5 bytes past the allocation and AddressSanitizer reports a heap-buffer-overflow at `src/H5Gnode.c:435`. The staged patch resolves this crash path by propagating the heap block size into the symbol-table B-tree lookup state and replacing crash-path `strcmp` uses with bounded `strncmp`/`strnlen`/`H5MM_strndup` operations.

source.description: First non-harness project statement on the witnessed path that consumes attacker-controlled local-heap header bytes and decodes the datablock extent into `heap->dblk_size`.
source.value_from: The fuzz harness writes the exact staged witness file `gt_results/arvo_42522531/poc` to `/tmp/libfuzzer.<pid>`, opens it with `H5Fopen`, and then requests dataset `"dsetname"`. On the saved run, root-group heap loading reaches `H5HL__hdr_deserialize`, and this decode reads the attacker-controlled local-heap header bytes from the file-backed cache image into `heap->dblk_size`. That size then drives the 88-byte `heap->dblk_image` allocation and the only offset bound checked before the crash-path compare.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. `H5G__node_cmp3` compares the fixed lookup name against a pointer into the heap-backed local-heap datablock with unbounded `HDstrcmp`, so a non-terminated heap suffix is read past the 88-byte allocation.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow` with `READ of size 5` in `strcmp`, then the first project frame at `src/H5Gnode.c:435`, and says the faulting address is 0 bytes to the right of the 88-byte region `[0x6080000002a0,0x6080000002f8)` allocated in `H5HL__cache_datablock_deserialize`.

root_cause.description: Missing string-extent check. `H5G__node_cmp3` treats a pointer into the local heap as a NUL-terminated string even though the only prior validation is `lt_key->offset < heap->dblk_size`; it never checks that a terminator exists within the remaining `heap->dblk_size - lt_key->offset` bytes before calling `HDstrcmp`.
root_cause.note: The fixing hunk adds `bt_udata.common.block_size = H5HL_heap_get_size(heap)` in `src/H5Gstab.c` and changes `H5G__node_cmp3` from `HDstrcmp` to `strncmp(udata->name, s, (udata->block_size - lt_key->offset))` on this left-side compare. Related patch hunks similarly replace other symbol-table `strcmp`/`strlen`/`strdup` uses with heap-size-bounded variants, which is the missing obligation on the witnessed path.

tainted_value_origin.description: The local-heap header decodes the attacker-controlled data-block extent later used both to allocate `heap->dblk_image` and to enforce the only offset guard before the unbounded compare.
tainted_value_origin.note: On the witnessed path, the decoded `heap->dblk_size` becomes the 88-byte extent later asserted equal to `len` in `H5HL__cache_datablock_deserialize` and reported by ASan as the overread source region.

parser_admitted.description: The staged HDF5 witness is admitted as a file because root-group opening succeeds here, so `H5Fopen` returns a valid file ID and the later dataset-open path reaches symbol-table lookup.
parser_admitted.condition: On the saved Stage 01 run, this error branch is not taken: `H5Fopen` succeeds, the harness then calls `H5Dopen2(fuzz_h5_id, "dsetname", H5P_DEFAULT)`, and the crash occurs during that dataset-name lookup.

fine_trace.note: The local-heap header decodes the attacker-controlled datablock size into `heap->dblk_size`. On the witnessed path, this extent later matches `len` and the 88-byte region AddressSanitizer reports as the overread source buffer.
Using the size from step 1, HDF5 allocates the heap-backed local-heap datablock. The saved ASan allocation stack identifies this call site as the 88-byte region later overread by the compare.

HDF5 copies the attacker-controlled local-heap datablock bytes from the file-backed cache image into `heap->dblk_image`. Those bytes become the symbol-table name storage later addressed by `H5HL_offset_into` and consumed by `HDstrcmp`.

Dataset-name lookup for the fixed search key `name == "dsetname"` pins the root group's symbol-table heap and passes the search name plus heap pointer into `H5B_find`'s comparator state. In the vulnerable source, no heap-block size is added here, so the later compare receives an interior heap pointer without any remaining-length bound. The B-tree compare will use a key offset from the symbol-table node together with this heap pointer.

fine_trace.code:
if (offset >= heap->dblk_size)
        HGOTO_ERROR(H5E_HEAP, H5E_CANTGET, NULL, "unable to offset into local heap data block");
fine_trace.note: Before exposing a symbol-table name pointer, HDF5 checks only that the requested heap offset is strictly inside the 88-byte local-heap buffer. On the crashing left-side compare, `lt_key->offset` satisfies this test, so lookup continues. This guard does not establish that a NUL terminator exists anywhere in the remaining `heap->dblk_image[offset .. heap->dblk_size-1]` bytes.

fine_trace.code:
if ((s = (const char *)H5HL_offset_into(udata->heap, lt_key->offset)) == NULL)
        HGOTO_ERROR(H5E_SYM, H5E_CANTGET, FAIL, "unable to get key name")
fine_trace.note: With step 5 accepted, the crash path resolves the left-side B-tree key's heap offset into pointer `s` inside the attacker-controlled local-heap bytes. `s` is now just an interior pointer; no length bound accompanies it into the subsequent comparison.

`H5G__node_cmp3` compares the fixed lookup name `udata->name` (`"dsetname"`) against heap pointer `s` with unbounded `HDstrcmp`. The only established precondition is step 5's offset-in-range check; there is no guard that `s` is NUL-terminated within the remaining `heap->dblk_size - lt_key->offset` bytes. On the saved run, the selected heap suffix is not terminated before the end of the 88-byte buffer, so the intercepted `strcmp` scans off the allocation. AddressSanitizer reports `READ of size 5` here, at the first byte just past the 88-byte region from step 2.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged `patch.diff` changes the crash path in `src/H5Gstab.c` and `src/H5Gnode.c`: lookup now records `bt_udata.common.block_size = H5HL_heap_get_size(heap)`, and `H5G__node_cmp3` replaces `HDstrcmp` with bounded `strncmp(..., udata->block_size - key->offset)`. Related hunks switch other symbol-table heap-string uses to bounded `strncmp`, `strnlen`, and `H5MM_strndup`, which resolves this missing-extent obligation.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: The allocation stack shows the overread source is the 88-byte `heap->dblk_image` buffer allocated in `H5HL__cache_datablock_deserialize`; the fine trace closes how `H5G__node_cmp3` later converts an in-range offset into a pointer inside that same buffer and then treats it as an unbounded C string after only an offset-in-range check.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run on `gt_results/arvo_42522531/poc` reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 5` in `strcmp -> H5G__node_cmp3 -> H5B_find`, matching both `sanitizer_trace.txt` and `reproduction_report.json`.

format.name: HDF5 file
format.contract: The verified trigger is the staged HDF5 witness file `gt_results/arvo_42522531/poc`. On the saved run, `H5Fopen` accepts it far enough to verify the root group and `H5Dopen2(..., "dsetname")` traverses the root symbol-table B-tree. Along that path, the root local-heap datablock is 88 bytes, the left-side symbol-table key offset used by `H5G__node_cmp3` points into a heap suffix that is not NUL-terminated before the block end, and the vulnerable code therefore calls `HDstrcmp` on a non-terminated heap pointer. The staged artifacts do not establish a broader class of malformed HDF5 layouts beyond this exact witness and crash path.
